answers.text:
Dear Sir or Madam,

I am writing you because your last bill is not correct and I am very angry for this situation. I am your customer since two year in Bradley Road and I never have a problem before.

Firstly, I open the bill of the last month and I see a new line in the middle. It is a extra service and I never ask this service to nobody. Nobody call me, nobody send me a e-mail, so I don't understand how it come in my bill. In my home we use only the internet for the computer and the television, nothing more. I think you have cheated me and this is not correct for a old customer.

Secondly, my connection is also very slow in the evening, but this is another problem and I write for it another time.

Thirdly, I want you to take out this line and give my money back to me. Please don't do this thing again to the customers.

I am waiting your answer, if not I must to change my company.

Regards,

Deniz Yilmaz

why_this_band.task_response: The first point is almost empty: there is no account number, invoice date, period or amount, so the company cannot locate the account from this letter. On top of that, the second paragraph strays outside the task with a speed complaint, and you have cheated me pulls the register away from a formal complaint.
why_this_band.coherence_cohesion: Firstly / Secondly / Thirdly marks the sequence, but since the second point carries an unrelated paragraph, the numbering becomes misleading. The sentences still follow one another, though, and the reader understands what the complaint is.
why_this_band.lexical_resource: Vocabulary for the bill is limited to bill, line, money back; the topic's own words such as charge, statement, refund never appear. Not correct is used twice for the same function, and the repetition stands out.
why_this_band.grammatical_range_accuracy: Most sentences have an error: I am writing you, since two year, a extra service, I never ask this service to nobody, nobody call me, how it come, I must to change. Structures are simple sentences and sequences added with and/so; there is very little subordination.

answers.what_would_lift_it: Put the details that identify the account at the start of the letter: account number, address, the invoice's date, period and the disputed amount. Removing the speed complaint entirely would also tighten the task response.

answers.text:
Dear Sir or Madam,

I am writing about my monthly bill for the internet connection at 14 Bradley Road. My account number is BR-4471902 and the bill is dated 3 September, for the period of August.

The total of this bill is 64.90 pounds, but until now I always paid 49.90 pounds every month. The reason of the difference is a line called Home Security Plus, which is 15 pounds. I have never asked for this service and nobody from your company contacted me about it, not by phone and not by e-mail. My contract from March last year includes only the broadband and the router rental, and I still have the copy of it.

I would be grateful if you can remove this charge from my account and send me a corrected bill for the period of August. As I already paid the full amount by direct debit on 10 September, I would like also the fifteen pounds to be returned to my account. Please can you confirm in writing that this service is cancelled and it will not appear on the next bills.

I look forward to hear from you within fourteen days.

Yours faithfully,

Deniz Yilmaz

why_this_band.task_response: All three points are addressed: the account and invoice are identified, the wrong item is shown with its name and amount, and the request has three parts (removal, a corrected bill, a refund). Why it was not requested stays a little brief; the contract is mentioned but the comparison with billing history is compressed into one sentence.
why_this_band.coherence_cohesion: The order is logical and does not strain the reader: identity, problem, request. However the third paragraph stacks three separate requests one after another, and apart from As I already paid no transition pattern is used, so the flow stays a little flat.
why_this_band.lexical_resource: The topic's own words, such as charge, corrected bill, direct debit, confirm in writing, are correctly used, and the register is formal. In places such as the reason of the difference and I look forward to hear from you, the form does not quite settle.
why_this_band.grammatical_range_accuracy: Relative clauses, time and reason clauses are controlled, and most sentences are error-free. The remaining errors (present perfect needed instead of I always paid, the reason of, I would like also, to hear from you) do not block meaning.

answers.what_would_lift_it: Tie why the item is wrong to evidence in one place: put what the contract covers next to the fact that this line never appeared on previous bills. This makes the request read as a conclusion rather than a claim.

answers.text:
Dear Sir or Madam,

I am writing about an incorrect charge on my most recent bill for the broadband service at 14 Bradley Road. The account number is BR-4471902 and the bill, dated 3 September, covers the billing period from 1 to 31 August.

The amount requested is 64.90 pounds, against the 49.90 pounds I have paid every month since the contract began in March last year. The difference is accounted for by a single line, Home Security Plus, charged at 15.00 pounds. I have never subscribed to this service. It does not appear in the contract I signed, which covers broadband and router rental only, nor on any of the seventeen bills I have received before this one, and no one from your company has contacted me by telephone or e-mail to offer it.

I would therefore ask you to remove the charge, cancel the service on the account, and issue a corrected bill for August. Since the full amount was taken by direct debit on 10 September, I would also be grateful if the fifteen pounds could be refunded to the same account rather than credited against future billing.

A written confirmation that the service has been cancelled would reassure me that the charge will not reappear. I should be glad to receive your reply within fourteen days, and I can be reached on 07700 900412 if any detail needs checking.

Yours faithfully,

Deniz Yilmaz

why_this_band.task_response: All three points are fully developed and the objection rests on three separate pieces of evidence: the contract, the previous seventeen bills, and the fact that no contact was ever made. The request is ordered and actionable, even the form of the refund is specified; the register stays measured and formal throughout.
why_this_band.coherence_cohesion: The letter follows the logic of an objection: identity, the difference in amount, evidence, request, response time. Therefore and Since do the work of the connectors, and the evidence sentence is brought together in a single structure with nor.
why_this_band.lexical_resource: The field's own words, such as billing period, accounted for by, subscribed to, credited against future billing, are used with the right collocation. The amount requested may sound a little formal, but it fits the context.
why_this_band.grammatical_range_accuracy: The passive, an inverted link with nor, and a conditional clause are controlled; punctuation and the format of numbers are consistent. Errors are rare and do not stop the reader, though the rhythm is not quite as easy as band 9 when two requests come one after another in the final paragraph.

answers.what_would_lift_it: Combine the two requests in the final paragraph into one sentence, and move the contact details to the closing sentence; the letter would deliver the same information in fewer moves.
